data.narrative:
Swift Solar, a Series C climate & energy company founded by Kevin Bush and five co-founders, is evaluated against a comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparator (LNZA). The target has raised $52.7M to date.

Two valuation methods anchor this analysis. Stage-progression, applying a typical 1.7x step-up multiplier to the $53M total raised proxy, yields $90M. Peer-median triangulation across three same-sector, same-stage companies—KoBold Metals ($3.0B), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B), and Amogy ($700M)—produces a median of $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B. The wide peer dispersion reflects heterogeneous capital intensity and commercialization timelines within frontier energy.

Synthesizing both methods produces a triangulated range of $76M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $545M. The stage-progression method anchors the lower bound, while peer medians support mid-to-upper valuation scenarios. Key uncertainties include Swift Solar's specific technology maturity relative to comps, path to commercialization, and capital efficiency versus peers. The $3.0B valuation ceiling (KoBold) and $700M floor (Amogy) suggest material sensitivity to perceived near-term revenue or deployment probability. Without disclosed financials or explicit comparable transaction multiples, the $545M median represents the central tendency but carries significant range around it.
